title: A new chapter: elections, handover and the first executive meetings
summary: The photobook follows NMA Ogun from the AGM and election into the opening meetings of the 2026–2028 administration.
paragraphs: NMA Ogun’s 2026 photobook opens with a sequence of photographs from the AGM and election, followed by the declaration of results. The captions identify the AGM and election day as 31 July. Together, the images introduce a new chapter in the association’s photographic record.

The record then moves to NMA House, Abeokuta. A group photograph is captioned as the inaugural State Officers Committee meeting on 4 August 2026. Another photograph records a handover by the past executive at NMA House.

A later photograph documents the first State Executive Council meeting with the newly elected SOC on 6 October 2026. Read together, these images record the progression from the election gathering to the early working meetings of the new administration. They offer members a way to revisit the people and settings connected with the transition.

This photo report accompanies the association’s leadership information. The current executives page remains the place to consult the published officer profiles, while the photobook preserves moments from the transition and meetings. Names, appointments and responsibilities should be read from the association’s published records rather than inferred from a person’s position in a group photograph.
Source: NMA Ogun Photobook 2026–2028, working edition, pages 2–4, 7–8 and 42.

title: NMA Ogun’s courtesy visit to the Commissioner of Police, in pictures
summary: Photographs document the association’s delegation at Eleweran, Abeokuta, on 14 August 2026.
paragraphs: The NMA Ogun photobook records a courtesy visit to the Ogun State Commissioner of Police at Eleweran, Abeokuta, on 14 August 2026. The two photographs provide complementary views of the engagement: a group photograph and a discussion around the meeting table.

Presented together, the photographs place the visit within the administration’s wider record of stakeholder engagements. The group image records the delegation at the venue; the meeting image captures the setting in which the discussion took place. The online album preserves the date and location given in the source captions.

For members following the association’s activities, a dated photographic record provides a useful point of reference. It identifies the occasion and makes it easier to connect a future formal report or communiqué with the event that it describes. It also helps preserve the association’s institutional memory beyond a single social-media update.

This article is a photographic account of the visit. Any detailed policy positions, undertakings or subsequent actions should be attributed to a corresponding published statement when available. Members seeking further information about the engagement can contact NMA Ogun State Secretariat.
Source: NMA Ogun Photobook 2026–2028, working edition, pages 11–12. Explore the advocacy and engagement album for other documented visits.

title: Across institutions: a photographic record of NMA Ogun’s engagements
summary: The working photobook brings together visits to government offices, health institutions and professional colleagues from August to October 2026.
paragraphs: NMA Ogun’s working photobook records a series of engagements across government offices, health institutions and the wider medical community. Rather than presenting these photographs as isolated images, the online collection brings them together as a dated visual record of the administration’s activities.

Photographs captioned 31 August 2026 include meetings with directors in the Ministry of Health and Hospital Management Board, and an engagement at the House of Assembly. The record continues with a visit to the Ogun State Head of Service on 9 September and photographs at the Medical Director’s office, Federal Medical Centre, Abeokuta, on 15 September.

The September sequence includes visits connected with the Ministry of Works and Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Aro, on 23 September. Photographs also document visits to senior professional colleagues and former NMA chairmen.

The October record includes the visit to Senator Salisu on 6 October and photographs with the Commissioner for Health, Dr Tomi Coker, dated 16 October 2026. These images sit alongside the association’s internal meetings and community activities, giving members a broader view of the occasions represented in the photobook.

The captions establish the occasions, people and dates recorded by the source. Formal outcomes or commitments should be read alongside an official report when one is published. This collection serves as a photographic record and a starting point for exploring the association’s work.
Source: NMA Ogun Photobook 2026–2028, working edition, selected pages from the August–October engagement sequence. Full captions and source-page links accompany the photographs.

title: World Mental Health Day: NMA Ogun’s outreach at Kuto Garage
summary: A photograph from the working photobook documents the outreach at Kuto Garage on 10 October 2026.
paragraphs: A photograph in the NMA Ogun photobook records a free outreach at Kuto Garage to mark World Mental Health Day on 10 October 2026. The image brings a community-facing activity into the administration’s wider visual record of meetings, visits and professional occasions.

The photograph shows members of the team at the outreach setting. Published with its caption and date, it gives visitors to the website a direct view of one of the activities documented in the working edition. It also provides an enduring reference for members who want to revisit the occasion after the original event notices have passed.

The website presents this image within a dedicated World Mental Health Day album and links it to the full photobook. This makes the outreach easier to find without requiring readers to download the entire publication or search through unrelated photographs.

The current source is a photographic record. Detailed information about the programme, participating services or a fuller activity report can be added when supplied by the organising team. Members with an approved report or additional captioned photographs can share them with the Secretariat for inclusion in the association’s public archive.
Source: NMA Ogun Photobook 2026–2028, working edition, page 51. The source caption identifies the occasion, venue and date.

title: Physicians’ Week 2026: the press conference in pictures
summary: The photobook records NMA Ogun’s Physicians’ Week press conference on 19 October 2026.
paragraphs: The NMA Ogun photobook includes a photograph captioned as the Physicians’ Week press conference on 19 October 2026. It forms part of a sequence that also documents the thanksgiving service and the “Saving the Savers” outreach.

The conference photograph records participants seated together beneath NMA signage. It gives the website’s Physicians’ Week archive a visual reference for the press engagement, alongside the published programme for the week. The activity date follows the caption supplied in the photobook.

The surrounding sequence begins with photographs of the thanksgiving service on 18 October and continues with outreach images dated 20 October. Bringing these occasions together helps members navigate the week as a connected programme while keeping the individual activities identifiable.

This photo report accompanies the visual archive. Readers seeking the association’s detailed statements should consult the corresponding published news reports or official communications. Additional approved conference photographs and a formal event report can be incorporated into the same archive as they become available.
Source: NMA Ogun Photobook 2026–2028, working edition, page 58. Explore the Physicians’ Week album for the related thanksgiving and outreach photographs.

title: “Saving the Savers”: moments from the Physicians’ Week outreach
summary: Team photographs and a presentation document the “Saving the Savers” medical outreach on 20 October 2026.
paragraphs: The closing sequence of the supplied NMA Ogun working photobook documents the “Saving the Savers” medical outreach on 20 October 2026. Three photographs record the outreach team and a presentation during the activity.

Two group photographs show the team gathered at the outreach setting, while the third captures a presentation. Their captions give the activity a name and date, allowing the images to be presented as a distinct part of the Physicians’ Week archive.

The photographs follow the thanksgiving service and press conference in the photobook’s October sequence. On the website, readers can move between those related activities, view the images at a larger size and consult the original publication through the source-page links.

This visual account preserves the team’s place in the association’s record of the week. It can be expanded with an approved narrative report from the organisers, including further programme details and documented outcomes. The current captions provide the basis for the information published here.

The wider photobook brings community activity, stakeholder visits and internal association meetings into one collection. The online albums make that collection easier to explore while retaining the original working edition as a reference.
Source: NMA Ogun Photobook 2026–2028, working edition, pages 59–61. The activity is dated 20 October 2026 in the source captions.
